profile.legal_name: Eastwood Homes (operating entities include Eastwood Construction LLC and Eastwood Construction Partners LLC)
profile.org_note: Family-owned and flat: founder Joe Stewart (now an advisor), President Clark Stewart (runs the company), CFO Kevin Hutchins, then division presidents by metro (11 divisions after the May 2026 Peachtree deal, about 450 employees). No regional layer is visible. Capital and deal decisions sit with the President and CFO; the CFO's conference bio credits him with securing financing and handling corporate and land acquisitions. Job-posting snippets point to a corporate VP of Land Development and a Chief Operating Officer, and to land acquisition managers inside divisions reporting to the division president; neither corporate role is named publicly.
profile.summary: Privately held, family-owned Charlotte builder founded 1977: about 1,500 closings a year in 140+ communities across NC, SC, VA and GA, plus a build-on-your-lot line; HousingWire ranks it the No. 11 private builder. Growing by acquisition: Napolitano Homes (Hampton Roads, March 2025) and Peachtree Building Group (Atlanta, May 2026, about 1,000 land, pipeline and work-in-progress assets). A conventional for-sale builder that funds itself with bank debt and family equity; its CFO speaks publicly on land-long versus land-light models and on bank versus private capital, which makes him the natural first call.

people.name: Kevin Hutchins
people.title: Chief Financial Officer
people.prior_role: Senior audit associate, Reznick, Fedder & Silverman (joined Eastwood 2003)
people.source_title: IMN Land & Homebuilding Capital Markets East speaker profile
people.note: Conference bio: oversees finance for Eastwood and its subsidiaries, has secured financing and handled corporate and land acquisitions; joined 2003 from Reznick, Fedder & Silverman; CPA. Quoted as Eastwood CFO on the Napolitano deal (The Builder's Daily, 2025-03-31). Listed as a speaker on bank vs private vs hybrid capital (IMN Residential Ground-Up Construction, 19-20 Nov 2026) and on land-long vs land-light models (IMN East, June 2027). The single finance and land-capital decision-maker visible in public sources. HousingWire (2026-05-27) interviewed him as the lead voice on the Peachtree deal, where he stressed being 'relevant to banking partners'.

people.name: Doug Cotter
people.title: Principal, Peachtree Building Group; Principal, Cotter Properties
people.source_title: HousingWire: Scale is now table stakes for private builders, Eastwood proves it
people.note: External partner, not an Eastwood land executive as far as public sources show: he and partner Scott Schmidt sold Peachtree Building Group to Eastwood, and Eastwood's CFO says Cotter Properties stays on as an active development partner in Atlanta. Listed here because he is the named source of developed lots for the Atlanta division. Title note: Peachtree Building Group was acquired May 2026; Cotter Properties is Eastwood's continuing Atlanta land development partner.

people.note: Company releases title him President and say the company is run by him; HousingWire (2026-05-26) calls him CEO. No separate CEO is named anywhere. Son of the founder; with the company since 2003 per a 2024 radio-station bio, which also mentions outside ventures in multifamily and cattle. Title note: Also described as CEO in trade press.

people.name: Joe Stewart

people.source_title: Eastwood Homes press release: Announces the Acquisition of Napolitano Homes
people.note: Joseph (Joe) Stewart founded the company in 1977 in Gastonia, NC. HousingWire (2026-05-27) reports he remains an advisor to the business; day-to-day leadership is with his son Clark Stewart. A public-records aggregator (Elementix) labels him 'Founder and Owner'; the ownership split within the family is not disclosed.
